# GEMM performance — sm_120 (NVIDIA RTX 5090)

<!-- The tables are generated by bench/gemm/python/render_perf_docs.py from tests/baselines/*.jsonl; do not edit them by hand. -->

Each row is one GEMM at one M, or in the grouped tables one grouped MoE GEMM over the experts of one projection, timed
alone in a CUDA graph with cold weights: the graph rotates through R copies of the weight, with R × weight bytes ≥ 2 ×
L2, and reports the replay time divided by R. BF16 is the unquantized reference, `torch.nn.functional.linear` on cuBLAS;
BSFP8 (block-scaled FP8) and MXFP8 are fso's GEMMs, each reported as µs per call, TFLOPS and `cos`, the cosine
similarity of its output against the BF16 output. In the grouped tables `m_cap` is the row capacity of each expert and
`weight GB/s` the rate at which the kernel reads the weights of the active experts. The grouped tables time
`fso.compat.linear_mxfp8_grouped_masked`, the grouped GEMM of the masked layout in which every expert has `m_cap` rows;
since 0.2.1 `fso.moe.layer` runs the compact layout's grouped GEMMs instead, so the whole-layer tables in
[`../layer/sm120.md`](../layer/sm120.md) are the cost a model pays. The RTX 5090 is clock-locked for the whole run with
`nvidia-smi -lgc 2407`, which reads 2400 MHz. The method is in [`../README.md`](../README.md), and the run that produced
each baseline file is named in its [Environments of record](../README.md#environments-of-record) block. Whole-layer
numbers and the comparisons against other libraries are in [`../layer/sm120.md`](../layer/sm120.md).
